holidays.name: International Harry Potter Day
holidays.description: Wizards, witches and Muggles around the world break out the wands, house scarves and butterbeer. They mark the day with movie marathons, trivia nights and themed treats.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the Battle of Hogwarts, the climactic showdown that ended the Second Wizarding War in the final Harry Potter story. Fans have celebrated it every May 2 since the books and films ended.
holidays.funFact: In 2012, British Prime Minister David Cameron was reported to have backed the day as a celebration of the series' lasting cultural impact.

holidays.name: National Play Your Ukulele Day
holidays.description: Dust off that four-stringed little guitar-lookalike and strum something sunny. Beginners are welcome, and so are off-key renditions. The ukulele is nearly impossible to play without smiling.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that began around 2011 to encourage people to pick up the ukulele and share its cheerful sound.
holidays.funFact: The word ukulele is often translated from Hawaiian as 'jumping flea,' a nod to how fast players' fingers dance across the fretboard.

holidays.name: National Truffle Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the earthy, aromatic fungus that chefs adore and wallets fear. Some people celebrate with truffle fries or pasta. Others go for chocolate truffles, which are just as good.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, celebrated every May 2.
holidays.funFact: Truffles grow underground and are traditionally found by trained dogs or pigs, and prized white truffles can sell for thousands of dollars per pound.
